instructionalPolicies.title: Academic Honesty
instructionalPolicies.summary:
Honesty is a necessary trait of all health care professionals, and KPSAHS expects all students to practice honest and ethical behavior. All forms of cheating or plagiarism are serious and will not be tolerated. KPSAHS reserves the right to use any process, including software, to determine if plagiarism has occurred. Any student who knowingly cheats, plagiarizes, or allows or aids another student in cheating or plagiarism will receive up to and including:
- a failing grade on a single assignment and/or final course grade
- suspension or dismissal from the program
The catalog defines plagiarism, cheating, fabrication, aiding/abetting dishonesty, and forgery.

instructionalPolicies.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI)
instructionalPolicies.summary: Faculty define the ethical use of AI for specific assignments on course syllabi and/or assignment instructions. Failing to follow the faculty member's definition of ethical and appropriate use of AI is considered a violation of the Academic Honesty Policy.

instructionalPolicies.title: Assessment and Student Record Holds
instructionalPolicies.summary:
Assessment is a fundamental part of the educational processes at KPSAHS. We continually strive to improve the institution's programs based on feedback from students, preceptors/clinical instructors, faculty, employers, and the communities we serve. Students will take part in assessment activities prior to, during, and/or upon completion of their education.
A hold may be placed on a student's record by the finance or assessment departments; see the Student Handbook for hold reasons and how to release them. Holds may prevent registration, viewing or printing schedules, receipt of a diploma, attendance in classes, or eligibility for graduation.

instructionalPolicies.title: Professional Ethics
instructionalPolicies.summary: All students are expected to follow the codes of professional ethics for their respective disciplines. These codes are reprinted in the Student Handbook.

instructionalPolicies.title: Intellectual Property
instructionalPolicies.summary: All lectures, presentations, and associated education materials used in any KPSAHS education program or created using KPSAHS resources are the intellectual property of KPSAHS, subject to applicable copyright laws. This material may not be copied, videotaped, or recorded without the written consent of the KPSAHS administration.

instructionalPolicies.title: Photographing or Recording Instruction
instructionalPolicies.summary:
- Classroom or lab instruction: photographs, video recordings, and/or audio recordings of lectures or lab activities are allowed at the discretion of the instructor or to meet documented ADA accommodations.
- Clinical instruction: photographs and recordings in the clinical setting require prior approval by the clinical instructor/preceptor, and all Kaiser Permanente patient privacy policies must be followed.
- Approved photographs and recordings are for personal academic use only; public posting, distribution, or any other use is prohibited.
KPSAHS may record classroom or online instructional activities without notification for educational evaluation or disciplinary action.

instructionalPolicies.title: Review of Examination Materials
instructionalPolicies.summary: All tests and examinations administered by KPSAHS instructors are the property of KPSAHS and may not be copied or altered except by KPSAHS personnel. At the discretion of the program, tests are available for review during the review session after an exam, during the review session before graduation, and during tutoring sessions with KPSAHS instructors. An instructor is present at all review sessions. Copying and/or altering tests will result in disciplinary action up to and including dismissal from any KPSAHS program.

instructionalPolicies.title: Electronic Devices and Wi-Fi
instructionalPolicies.summary: Use of electronic devices in the classroom, including cell phones, tablets, and laptops, is at the discretion of the instructor. Use of Wi-Fi in the classroom is also at the instructor's discretion, is for educational purposes only, and requires agreeing to the Acceptable Use Policy at login.

instructionalPolicies.title: Classroom Equipment
instructionalPolicies.summary: Students are not allowed to operate any video conferencing or electronic equipment in any KPSAHS classroom, including the video conferencing control console, PC, document camera, and DVD, except when presenting under the direct supervision of the instructor (the instructor physically present in the room). Students who do not follow this policy will be immediately suspended and may face further disciplinary action up to and including dismissal.

instructionalPolicies.title: Email Communications
instructionalPolicies.summary: The official method of communication between students and KPSAHS faculty and staff is the KPSAHS-issued email account (if available) or the email account the student provided during enrollment or in the student portal. Students are required to set up and maintain their email accounts and should check email frequently.

instructionalPolicies.title: Online Learning
instructionalPolicies.summary:
## Learning management system
Students are oriented to the KPSAHS learning management system, KPScholar, during program orientation. Any student not familiar with it will be given access and instruction by the Department of Instructional Innovation and Digital Learning or assigned faculty.
## Instructor response time
Students in KPSAHS distance education courses should expect a response or evaluation for all lessons and projects within ten calendar days of the instructor receiving the submission.
## Required equipment
- laptop or desktop running Windows 7 or higher or Mac OS 10.10 or higher (Chromebooks will likely work but may not be consistent enough)
- Intel i3 or equivalent processor, 2 GHz or higher
- 2 GB RAM minimum; 4 GB or higher recommended
- an up-to-date browser such as Chrome or Firefox
- broadband internet with at least 2 Mbps download and upload speeds
- webcam and microphone (a headset with microphone is recommended)
- Microsoft Office Suite

instructionalPolicies.title: Laboratory Coursework
instructionalPolicies.summary: Laboratory courses may require students to serve as volunteer patients for the practice of clinical skills. Serving as a patient is voluntary, and students' grades and evaluations will not be affected by their participation or non-participation. Students who decline must still complete all required procedures in the laboratory classroom. Should a large number of students decline to volunteer as patients, classroom hours may be extended.

instructionalPolicies.title: Clinical Education Policies
instructionalPolicies.summary:
While in clinical education, students follow KPSAHS and clinical facility policies and procedures, including:
- accept no gratuities from patients, and inform the instructor/school of any attendance issues
- get permission from the preceptor/clinical instructor before leaving the clinical site
- never discuss patient information in public, or a patient's condition with other patients
- give no medication, water, or treatment except under the direction of a physician
- wear the photo ID badge at all times on school or clinical site property, and a radiation dosimetry badge if applicable
Clinical assignments are made by the clinical coordinator with the program director, and students may need to travel long distances or rotate between sites. Students in the baccalaureate, phlebotomy, bone densitometry, and medical assisting programs must hold a current American Heart Association BLS CPR card to participate in clinical education. Radiation safety requirements are in the Student Handbook.

instructionalPolicies.title: Disability Accommodations (ADA)
instructionalPolicies.summary:
KPSAHS provides individuals with disabilities equal educational opportunities, programs, and services. Students should request reasonable accommodations as soon as possible after acceptance. Documentation must be current (no more than five years old) and from a qualified professional.
## How to request accommodations
- Meet with the dean of academic affairs to provide the required documentation. To have accommodations in place for the current quarter, give notice with all required materials within the first two weeks of the quarter.
- Accommodations cannot be applied retroactively to previous coursework.
- Approved accommodations are documented in a KPSAHS Letter of Accommodation. Give a copy to your instructors at the beginning of every term.
- If you feel your accommodations are not being met, contact the program director or the dean of academic affairs.
